On Wed, Feb 6, 2013 at 11:11 AM, Yann Richet <riche...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi (Joe :),

I wish to provide editing feature on a dataset located on server side.

So here, it works well (without server-side editing) :
========= ui.R =========
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(  
  headerPanel("Title2"),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(
    h2("edit"),
    tags$textarea(id="texteditor","functionnnn foo(items) {\n    var x = \"All this is syntax highlighted\";\n    return x;\n}"),
    tags$div(id="aceeditor"),
    HTML(readLines("www/autoselect.js"),
    h2("result"),
    textOutput("debug")
  )
))
==========================
========= server.R ==========
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$debug <- reactiveText(function() {
    input$texteditor
  })
})
==========================
======= autoselect.js =========
<style type="text/css" media="screen">
    #aceeditor { 
    height: 275px;
    position: relative;
    border: 1px solid #DDD;
    border-radius: 4px;
    border-bottom-right-radius: 0px;
    margin-top: 5px;
    }
</style>
<script src="http://d1n0x3qji82z53.cloudfront.net/src-min-noconflict/ace.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8"></script>
<script>
    var aceeditor = ace.edit("aceeditor");
    aceeditor.setTheme("ace/theme/twilight");
    aceeditor.getSession().setMode("ace/mode/javascript");
    
    var texteditor = $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide();
aceeditor.getSession().setValue(texteditor.val());

aceeditor.getSession().on('change', function(e){
  texteditor.val(aceeditor.getSession().getValue());
  texteditor.change();
});
    texteditor.onchange = function() {
        texteditor.select();
    };
</script>
==========================


Now, if I wish to provide server-side editing using uiOutput (in place of tags$textarea) :
========= ui.R =========
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(  
  headerPanel("Title2"),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(
    h2("edit"),
    uiOutput("textarea"),
    tags$div(id="aceeditor"),
    HTML(readLines("www/autoselect.js"),
    h2("result"),
    textOutput("debug")
  )
)))
==========================
========= server.R ==========
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$debug <- reactiveText(function() {
    input$texteditor
  })
  output$textarea <- reactiveUI(function() { 
    return(
      tags$textarea(id="texteditor",(paste(readLines(file.path("test.R")),collapse="\n")))
    )
  })
})
==========================

it seems that the textarea element is not found by jquery selector in autoselect.js (line "var texteditor = $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide();")

Any idea ?

Le jeudi 7 février 2013 14:10:31 UTC+1, Yann Richet a écrit :
Thank you Joe for this suggestion, but it did not fix the issue.
In fact, it seems that the uiOutput("textarea") is not evaluated at the startup of the page, so the jquery $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide(); is not applied (as well as replacing by textarea#texteditor).

I tried to use a jquery plugin name livequery, so the hide() will be applied as soon as the <div id="textarea"><textarea>...</div> appears, but without success. It seems that the jquery plugin is not loaded.
As I am a beginner in jquery, I suspect it is not related to shiny :)

Anyway, I finally turnaround the issue with the following change in autoselect.js (whcih should be renamed by the way) :
======= autoselect.js =========
<style type="text/css" media="screen"> #aceeditor { height: 300px; position: relative; border: 1px solid #DDD; border-radius: 4px; border-bottom-right-radius: 0px; margin-top: 5px; } </style> <script src="http://d1n0x3qji82z53.cloudfront.net/src-min-noconflict/ace.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8"></script> <script> var aceeditor = ace.edit("aceeditor"); aceeditor.setTheme("ace/theme/twilight"); aceeditor.getSession().setMode("ace/mode/javascript"); $("div").on('mouseenter',function(e) { var texteditor = $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide(); aceeditor.getSession().setValue(texteditor.val()); aceeditor.getSession().on('change',function(e) { texteditor.val(aceeditor.getSession().getValue()); texteditor.change(); }); }); </script>
==========================
this is quite ugly, because the textarea is initally visible (and also the  $("div").on('mouseenter',function(e) {} seems like a hammer), but it is a little bit better...

If you have any idea on how to use livequery, I am interested.

messages.subject: Re: Including ACE with content from server side
parts:
Thank you Joe.
Well, it seems it is needed on both ui and server side. If I just put it on server side (inside reactiveUI return), the ace editor is not well instanciated.

To close the topic, here is a working solution:
================ ui.R
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(  
  headerPanel("Title3"),

sidebarPanel(),
  
  mainPanel(
    h2("edit"),
    uiOutput("textarea"),
    tags$div(id="aceeditor"),

HTML(readLines("www/autoselect.js")),
    #HTML(readLines("www/jquery.livequery.js")),

h2("result"),
    textOutput("debug")
  )
))

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
    
  
  output$debug <- reactiveText(function() {
    input$texteditor
  })
  
  
  output$textarea <- reactiveUI(function() { 
    return(

tags$div(tags$textarea(id="texteditor",(paste(readLines(file.path("test.R")),collapse="\n"))),HTML(readLines("www/autoselect.js")))
    )
  })
  
})
=================
================ www/autoselect.js

<style type="text/css" media="screen">
    #aceeditor { 
    height: 300px;
    position: relative;
    border: 1px solid #DDD;
    border-radius: 4px;
    border-bottom-right-radius: 0px;
    margin-top: 5px;
    }
</style>
<script src="http://d1n0x3qji82z53.cloudfront.net/src-min-noconflict/ace.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8"></script>
<script> 

  var aceeditor = ace.edit("aceeditor");
  aceeditor.setTheme("ace/theme/twilight");
  aceeditor.getSession().setMode("ace/mode/javascript");

  $("div").on('mouseenter',function(e) {
    var texteditor = $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide();
        
    aceeditor.getSession().setValue(texteditor.val());
    
    aceeditor.getSession().on('change',function(e) {
//$("button#save").on('click',function(e) {

texteditor.val(aceeditor.getSession().getValue());
      texteditor.change();
    });
    
  });
</script>

=================

Note that I also use the on('change' instead of the $("button#save").on('click', because it seems to not work properly.
(and I definitely don't understand why.)

Le jeudi 7 février 2013 14:10:31 UTC+1, Yann Richet a écrit :
Thank you Joe for this suggestion, but it did not fix the issue.
In fact, it seems that the uiOutput("textarea") is not evaluated at the startup of the page, so the jquery $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide(); is not applied (as well as replacing by textarea#texteditor).

I tried to use a jquery plugin name livequery, so the hide() will be applied as soon as the <div id="textarea"><textarea>...</div> appears, but without success. It seems that the jquery plugin is not loaded.
As I am a beginner in jquery, I suspect it is not related to shiny :)

Anyway, I finally turnaround the issue with the following change in autoselect.js (whcih should be renamed by the way) :
======= autoselect.js =========
<style type="text/css" media="screen"> #aceeditor { height: 300px; position: relative; border: 1px solid #DDD; border-radius: 4px; border-bottom-right-radius: 0px; margin-top: 5px; } </style> <script src="http://d1n0x3qji82z53.cloudfront.net/src-min-noconflict/ace.js" type="text/javascript" charset="utf-8"></script> <script> var aceeditor = ace.edit("aceeditor"); aceeditor.setTheme("ace/theme/twilight"); aceeditor.getSession().setMode("ace/mode/javascript"); $("div").on('mouseenter',function(e) { var texteditor = $('textarea[id="texteditor"]').hide(); aceeditor.getSession().setValue(texteditor.val()); aceeditor.getSession().on('change',function(e) { texteditor.val(aceeditor.getSession().getValue()); texteditor.change(); }); }); </script>
==========================
this is quite ugly, because the textarea is initally visible (and also the  $("div").on('mouseenter',function(e) {} seems like a hammer), but it is a little bit better...

If you have any idea on how to use livequery, I am interested.
